content: Dr. Ahmad Tibi, also spelled Ahmed Tibi, was born on December 19, 1958. He is an Israeli Arab politician and the leader of the Arab nationalist party Ta'al, also known as the Arab Movement for Renewal. He was elected to the Israeli parliament, the Knesset, on a joint ticket with the United Arab List. Dr. Tibi identifies as Arab-Palestinian by nationality but has referred to Israel as his homeland and has pledged to remain in Israel regardless of the future of the Palestinian territories. He hails from Taibeh, located in Israel's Central District. Dr. Tibi is a trained physician and graduated from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. During his early career, Dr. Tibi worked as a resident at Hadassah Hospital, which is known for fostering positive Jewish-Arab relations. However, these relations were tested when he struck a security guard on the head with his briefcase, causing an injury that required stitches. He walked away while the guard bled on the floor. Dr. Tibi was dismissed from his position a few hours later. He contested his dismissal, claiming it was due to his Arab identity and arguing that the guard should have shown more respect to a doctor. The hospital maintained that Dr. Tibi had refused to allow his briefcase to be searched and that the guard was simply performing his duties. Dr. Tibi served as a political advisor to the late Palestinian Authority Chairman Yasser Arafat for several years. He even represented the Palestinians during the 1998 Wye River negotiations. In 1999, he resigned from his advisory role to run for the Knesset. Dr. Tibi described his relationship with Arafat as close and extremely interesting and important. He was first elected to the Knesset in 1999 as a member of Azmi Bishara's Balad party but later broke away to form his own party, Ta'al, during the Knesset session. In 2002, right-wing Knesset member Michael Kleiner initiated actions to restrict Dr. Tibi's movements within the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, accusing him of aiding Palestinians in their conflict against Israel. Dr. Tibi protested these restrictions, calling them unconstitutional and illegal under Israeli law. He appealed to the Supreme Court of Israel, which deferred its decision on the matter. Ahead of the 2003 Israeli elections, several right-wing politicians, including leaders of the National Union and National Religious Party, sought to disqualify Dr. Tibi from holding Knesset office. Likud Knesset member Michael Eitan officially filed a motion to disqualify Dr. Tibi's candidacy, which narrowly passed the Israeli Central Elections Committee by one vote. Eitan accused Dr. Tibi of supporting Palestinian terrorism during the intifada and of using his Knesset immunity to promote Palestinian and Arafat's interests. He further alleged that Dr. Tibi had engaged in anti-Israeli activities, including expressing solidarity with Israel's enemies, incitement, and sedition. However, the Supreme Court of Israel unanimously overturned the ban, allowing Dr. Tibi to run for office. He was subsequently elected as part of a joint list of Ta'al and Hadash. Before the 2006 elections, Dr. Tibi withdrew his Ta'al party from the Hadash coalition and joined the United Arab List. He currently serves as a Deputy Speaker of the Knesset.
